assumptions: PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, S3, and Reset are modeled as discrete events rather than persistent boolean variables, following the trigger/signal wording.
hbrg is encoded as an integer output: 0 for stop at floor states, 1 for upward drive in MU2/MU3, and -1 for downward drive in MD1/MD2.

The immediate next-destination check after arrival is represented by event-triggered outgoing transitions from each floor state; no additional queue or request-memory variables were introduced because they were not specified.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init probe: dispatches initial [*] to F1, then checks F1->MU2->F2 and immediate next request F2->MU3->F3 with hbrg stop/up outputs.
scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_then_up_to_f2_and_f3

scenario_results.description: default-init probe: after initial F1 dispatch, PS3 selects MU3, S3 stops at F3, then PS2 selects downward MD2 and S2 stops at F2.
scenario_results.name: f1_direct_to_f3_then_down_to_f2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: from reachable floor F2, PS1 must select downward MD1 and S1 arrival must stop at F1.
scenario_results.name: f2_request_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: from reachable floor F3, PS1 must select downward MD1 rather than MD2, and S1 arrival must stop at F1.
scenario_results.name: f3_request_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: Reset during an upward motion context must force F1 and stop hbrg regardless of outstanding request context.
scenario_results.name: reset_forces_f1_from_up_motion

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: Reset during a downward motion context must force F1 and stop hbrg regardless of outstanding request context.
scenario_results.name: reset_forces_f1_from_down_motion

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probe: Reset from a non-F1 floor context must still force the controller back to F1 with stop hbrg.
scenario_results.name: reset_forces_f1_from_floor_context

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start no-fire probe: a motion state should not complete arrival without its required sensing input, so MU2 remains in upward drive on an empty cycle.
scenario_results.name: motion_states_wait_without_arrival_sensor

evidence: NL requires floor states F1/F2/F3 and motion states MU2/MU3/MD1/MD2; DSL defines all seven leaf states.
NL requires F1->MU2 on PS2, F1->MU3 on PS3, F2->MU3 on PS3, F2->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD2 on PS2; DSL contains each transition.
NL requires MU2+S2->F2, MU3+S3->F3, MD1+S1->F1, MD2+S2->F2; DSL contains each arrival transition.
NL requires reset force to floor 1 regardless of context; DSL uses '! * -> F1 :: Reset'.
NL says hbrg distinguishes upward drive, downward drive, and stop; DSL assigns 1 in MU2/MU3, -1 in MD1/MD2, and 0 in F1/F2/F3.
findings.summary: The DSL is faithful to the explicit elevator FSM requirements: required floor states, motion states, request-triggered dispatches, sensor-triggered arrivals, reset-to-F1 behavior, and hbrg drive/stop encoding are present.

evidence: GroundingMap lists required states, events PS1/PS2/PS3/S1/S2/S3/Reset, required transitions, and hbrg actions.
inspect_model_to_json_summary reports 7 leaf states, 7 events, 1 variable, and 18 total transitions including forced reset expansion.
sim_summary reports 8/8 scenarios passed, covering normal upward/downward routes, reset from motion/floor states, and no-arrival wait behavior.
findings.summary: Core components are covered: states, input events, transitions, initial state, reset behavior, and output actions are all represented.

evidence: DSL has only one variable, hbrg, which is an output and not a request-memory variable.
GroundingMap source_summary states: 'no additional queue or request-memory variables were introduced because they were not specified.'
NL says the controller 'immediately checks the next destination' and reset acts 'regardless of the outstanding request context'.
findings.summary: The model does not explicitly represent request memory, queued outstanding requests, or simultaneous/multiple pending destinations. This is acceptable for the stated transition-level requirements but remains a semantic coverage limitation because the NL mentions outstanding request context and immediate next-destination checking.

evidence: DSL floor states F1/F2/F3 stop on entry and wait for PS events.
There are no internal guards or variables representing pending destinations.
This matches the explicit listed transitions but abstracts away any automatic queue-processing semantics.
findings.summary: The 'immediate next-destination check' is modeled as event-triggered outgoing transitions from floor states rather than an explicit internal decision or automatic dispatch based on stored requests.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary contains advisory W_UNREFERENCED_VAR: 'Variable hbrg does not affect any transition guard.'
NL defines hbrg as an output distinguishing drive and stop conditions.
DSL assigns hbrg in state entry actions and does not need it to affect transition guards.
findings.summary: The W_UNREFERENCED_VAR warning for hbrg is not a semantic defect here because hbrg is used as a pure output, not as a guard variable.

evidence: current_dsl retains 'def int hbrg = 0;' and all entry assignments.
warning_budget_exhausted is empty.
design_diagnostics_summary shows repair_count 0 for W_UNREFERENCED_VAR.
findings.summary: No unjustified warning repair is evident; the output variable hbrg was retained despite the advisory unreferenced-variable warning, which is appropriate for a pure output.

evidence: No blocking design diagnostics are reported.
sim_summary ok=true with 8/8 scenarios passed.
GroundingMap covers all explicit NL states, inputs, transitions, reset, and hbrg actions.
The remaining request-context abstraction is minor rather than T0/T1 empty-shell or low-coverage behavior.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate. No quality cap is warranted because the required state/transition/action structure is present and exercised by passing simulations; only minor abstraction limits remain around request memory.

evidence: GroundingMap source_summary explicitly records the assumption that no queue/request-memory variables were introduced.
DSL separates only control state and hbrg output; it has no internal destination memory.
The explicit transition list in the NL is fully implemented, making this an interpretation boundary rather than a missing listed transition.
findings.summary: The residual coverage limitation likely comes from choosing the simpler event-triggered FSM interpretation of floor requests instead of introducing an explicit request-context component, due to the NL not specifying queue semantics in detail.
